etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From rudiment +‎ -ary (adjectival suffix), perhaps after New Latin rudīmentārius, from Classical Latin rudīmentum (“first attempt; beginning”) + -ārius (adjectival suffix). Compare French rudimentaire.
senses: Of or relating to one or more rudiments; of the nature of an early stage.
(zoology, usually in the plural) One of the rudimentary (adjective sense 1) mammae of boars.
